title: School Bell
blurb: Harsh, unmusical, and in charge of childhood for well over a century. The bell triggers something deep in anybody who has ever owned a locker: an involuntary urge to stand and leave, regardless of what is currently being said. The reflex does not decay with age. Play it midway through a meeting and grown adults will visibly start packing up before they catch themselves. It also works beautifully over edits about escapes, deadlines and freedom, all three of which it has always meant at once.
